fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Into a Scored Quiz
fields.features_subheading: A scored quiz adds up the points from each answer and turns the total into a result. Emergent builds both from a prompt.
fields.feature_1:
A point value on every question

Tell Emergent which questions matter more, such as 2 points for each safety question and 1 for the rest. The top score and the pass mark update whenever a weight changes.
fields.feature_2:
A result screen for each band

Split the score range into bands, such as 0 to 9, 10 to 15, and 16 to 20, and give each one its own title and message. Players see theirs right after the last answer.
fields.feature_3:
Partial credit where it is fair

Select-all questions can earn a point for each correct pick instead of all or nothing. Decide whether a wrong pick costs a point; the app never scores a question below 0.
fields.feature_4:
An alert when someone misses the mark

Pick a pass mark, and the app emails the trainer or posts to a Slack channel with the name of each person who scored under it. Reminders follow until the retake is done.
fields.feature_5:
Every answer kept with its points

Each answer is saved as a row in a database you own, with the points it earned. Sort by question to find the one that costs players the most, then rewrite it before round 2.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain and the full code

Run the quiz on your own domain; custom domains are included in Emergent and use credits. Paid plans export the full code to your GitHub repository for a developer to extend.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Scored Quizzes, Four Point Rules
fields.tab_content_1:
Each of the 5 fire questions is worth 2 points

Every new front desk hire at Grayhaven Hotels takes a 15-question training quiz. The 5 questions on the fire evacuation route are worth 2 points each, so the top score is 20 and the pass mark is 16. In March, 9 of the 48 new hires scored under 16. Gethin Strakosch got an email naming all 9, and they retook it on Friday.
fields.tab_content_2:
Visitors at 70 or more go to Slack for a call

Visitors to Lumbard Studio's site answer 10 questions about their website, each worth 0 to 10 points, for a score out of 100. A score of 70 or more posts to the studio's Slack channel, and Renske Junot calls that visitor. In September, 412 visitors finished the quiz, and 58 of them scored 70 or more.
fields.tab_content_3:
Of 51 who pass, 7 owe it to partial credit

Twenty of the 25 questions on Vinterra Wine School's certificate exam are worth 1 point. The other 5 are select-all questions with 3 right picks each, a point per pick. The exam is worth 35 points, and the pass mark is 28. This spring, 51 of the 64 students passed. Without partial credit, 7 of those 51 would have fallen short.
fields.tab_content_4:
The final round counts double for all 14 teams

On Thursdays, 14 teams play trivia at Hopstead Brewing: 6 rounds of 8 questions, with round 6 worth 2 points a question, for 56 points in all. The leaderboard on the bar's TV updates as soon as the host closes a round. Last Thursday, Barley Brains trailed Last Call Club by 3 points after round 5 and won with 47.

fields.howto_title: How to Make a Scored Quiz
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to make a scored quiz whose points, pass mark, and result bands hold up before anyone takes it.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Decide what the score is for
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Give each question a point value
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Decide what a wrong answer costs
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Set bands that cover every score
fields.howto_step_1_des: Say what happens with each score before you write a question: a pass or a retake, a group placement, or a sales call. Put that in your prompt, and Emergent builds the quiz and its result screens around it.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Weight the questions that matter most. On a 15-question quiz where 5 safety questions carry 2 points each, the maximum is 20 points, and a player who misses all 5 safety questions cannot reach a pass mark of 16.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Zero is the plain choice for a wrong answer. Take a point off only where guessing is a real problem, and tell players before they start, since a penalty changes how they answer.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Split the range into 2 to 4 bands and write each edge as a number, never as a vague word like high. Then check that every possible score lands in exactly one band, including 0 and the maximum.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Write one result screen per band
fields.howto_step_5_des: Give each band a title and one next step, such as a retake date or a booking link to a call. Add the correct answers under it, and players can see exactly where their points went.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Run 3 test players through it: one who answers everything right, one who answers everything wrong, and one who lands exactly on the pass mark. Each should reach the screen you expect, with the right score saved.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Fix the question that costs most
fields.howto_step_7_des: After the first 50 players, sort the answer table by question. Reread the wording of any question that nearly everyone misses before you change its points or move the pass mark.

faq_plan.a: A scored quiz is a quiz that gives points for each answer, adds them into a total, and shows every player a result based on that total. Questions can carry different point values, and the total can decide who passes, which group a player joins, or which follow-up they get.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a scored quiz?
faq_plan.a: Describe it in a prompt to Emergent's AI survey builder, with the points for each question and the pass mark. Emergent builds the quiz and the database behind it, and you change any rule by prompting again. The free tier covers building and publishing.

faq_plan.q: How do you turn a scored quiz result into a percentage?
faq_plan.a: Divide the points earned by the points possible, then multiply by 100: a player with 17 of 20 points scores 85. On a weighted quiz, count points, not right answers. A player with 12 right answers can hold 14 points or 18, depending on which questions they got.

faq_plan.q: Should a scored quiz take points off for wrong answers?
faq_plan.a: No, not by default. Take points off only when a lucky guess could change the result, such as on a certification exam with a pass mark. If you do, tell players before the first question, and set a floor of 0 so one question never drags the total down.

faq_plan.q: How many questions should a scored quiz have?
faq_plan.a: Aim for 8 to 15 questions on a quiz people take by choice, such as a lead quiz on a website, and use as many as the material needs on a pass or fail test. More questions mean each one counts for less, and one badly worded question moves the result less.

faq_plan.q: How do I choose a pass mark for a scored quiz?
faq_plan.a: Set the pass mark at the lowest score you would accept from someone who knows the material, then test it against real answers. If a topic is essential, weight its questions so that missing all of them makes a pass impossible. The app Emergent builds keeps every answer in a database you own, where you can count how many players landed 1 point under the mark.

faq_plan.q: Can a scored quiz give partial credit?
faq_plan.a: Yes. On a select-all question, each right pick can be worth a point on its own, and a ranking or matching question can award a point for every item in the right place. Write the rule into the question's instructions. Players who know a half-right answer still counts are less likely to skip it.

faq_plan.q: What is the difference between a scored quiz and an outcome quiz?
faq_plan.a: A scored quiz adds up points and places the total in a score band; an outcome quiz maps each answer to a result and shows the one picked most often. Use a scored quiz when answers can be right or wrong, or rated on a scale, and an outcome quiz when every answer is valid and you want to sort people by preference.

faq_plan.q: How do I use a scored quiz to qualify leads?
faq_plan.a: Give each answer points for how closely it fits your buyer, add them up, and send every score above a threshold to sales. A team of 50 might earn 10 points where a team of 2 earns 2. Emergent builds the quiz with Slack and email alerts. A high score can reach the person who makes the call while the lead is still on your site.

faq_plan.q: Can players see their scored quiz answers at the end?
faq_plan.a: Yes, if you choose to show them. The result screen can list each question with the player's answer, the correct one, and the points earned. Show them on a practice quiz, and hide them on an exam people can retake. That way the second try still tests what they remember.

quiz.title: Can You Score This Scored Quiz by Hand?
quiz.intro: Eight questions on points, pass marks, wrong-answer penalties, and score bands. Work each one out, then see how your own total lands.

questions.text: A 10-question quiz gives 1 point per right answer. A player gets 7 right. What is the score as a percentage?
questions.explanation: Divide points earned by points possible and multiply by 100: 7 / 10 x 100 = 70.

questions.text: A quiz has 12 questions worth 1 point and 4 questions worth 2 points. What is the highest possible score?
questions.explanation: The 12 one-point questions give 12, and the 4 two-point questions give 8. 12 + 8 = 20.

questions.text: On that same 20-point quiz, the pass mark is 80 percent of the points. How many points does a player need to pass?
Each right answer earns 1 point and each wrong answer loses 0.25. Blanks score 0. A player has 14 right, 4 wrong, and 2 blank. Score?
questions.explanation: 14 right gives 14, and 4 wrong take away 4 x 0.25 = 1. The 2 blanks add nothing. 14 - 1 = 13.

questions.text: A select-all question has 3 right options. A right pick earns 1, a wrong pick loses 1, and 0 is the floor. Picks: 2 right, 1 wrong. Score?
questions.explanation: 2 right picks earn 2, and the 1 wrong pick takes 1 away. 2 - 1 = 1, which is above the floor of 0.

questions.text: A 20-point quiz has three result bands: 0 to 9, 10 to 14, and 16 to 20. Which score has no result screen?
questions.explanation: The second band ends at 14 and the third starts at 16, so a player who scores exactly 15 falls between them.

questions.text: Part A has 30 questions worth 1 point. Part B has 10 questions worth 3 points. What share of the total points comes from Part B?
questions.explanation: Part A is worth 30 points and Part B is worth 10 x 3 = 30. The total is 60, and 30 / 60 = 0.5, or 50 percent.

questions.text: Five players score 12, 15, 18, 9, and 16 points. What is the average score?

results.title: Time for a Recount
results.description: You scored 0 to 3. Weighted points and penalties are easy to trip on. Before you launch a scored quiz, write the maximum score and the pass mark down and test a perfect run, a zero, and a run that lands exactly on the mark.

results.title: Steady Scorekeeper
results.description: You scored 4 to 6. You can add up a weighted quiz, and the misses are in the edge cases: penalties, partial credit, or a gap between bands. Check those three before your quiz goes live.

results.title: Ready to Run the Scoring
results.description: You scored 7 or 8. You can weight questions, set a pass mark, and spot a missing band. Put those rules in a prompt, and the quiz you build can do the adding up for every player.

plan.angle: Searchers for a scored quiz want to know how the points turn into a result: what each question is worth, where the pass mark sits, and what each score band shows. This page lets them score 8 quiz questions by hand on the page, then shows four scored quizzes a hotel, a design studio, a wine school, and a taproom run as their own app, each with its own point rule, and a seven-step method for weighting, banding, and testing the scoring before launch.
tab_stories: Grayhaven Hotels gives 48 new front desk hires a 15-question training quiz where the 5 fire evacuation questions are worth 2 points each, so the top score is 20 and the pass mark is 16; 9 fall short and training lead Gethin Strakosch gets an email naming them before Friday's retake.

Lumbard Studio puts a 10-question website readiness quiz on its site, each answer worth 0 to 10 points; 412 visitors finished it in September, and the 58 who scored 70 or more posted to Slack for Renske Junot to call.

Vinterra Wine School runs a 25-question certificate exam worth 35 points, with 5 select-all questions that give a point per correct pick; 51 of 64 students reach the 28-point pass mark, 7 of them only because of partial credit.

Hopstead Brewing runs trivia night as 6 rounds of 8 questions with the last round worth double, for 56 points in all; the leaderboard on the bar TV updates after each round, and Table Nine wins 14 teams with 47 points.
